```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,

theme_measure_sec <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white")
    )
}
```

## Scope

The SEC QC functions calculate resolution, plate count, asymmetry, recovery,
and replicate precision from supplied peak data. The acceptance criteria are
provided by the analyst or taken from the function's defaults; they are not
selected or validated by the package.

`sec_system_suitability` is a synthetic teaching dataset. Its `expected_*`
columns are generated scenario values, not metrics calculated from the raw
traces. The dataset contains a sequence of column-age scenarios, not replicate
injections, so it cannot show repeatability.

## Synthetic column-age example

```{r setup}
library(measure.sec)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r system-data}
data(sec_system_suitability, package = "measure.sec")

run_summary <- sec_system_suitability |>
  distinct(
    run_id,
    column_age_days,
    expected_plate_count,
    expected_resolution
  ) |>
  arrange(column_age_days)

run_metrics <- run_summary |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(expected_plate_count, expected_resolution),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "expected_value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      expected_plate_count = "Expected plate count (N, plates)",
      expected_resolution = "Expected resolution (Rs)"
    )
  )

run_metrics
```

The dashed lines below use the current default values in
`measure_sec_suitability()` for plate count and resolution. They show how the
software compares values with supplied criteria; they are not regulatory
limits or a qualification decision.

```{r system-suitability-trend, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Generated plate-count and resolution values across the synthetic column-age scenarios. Dashed lines mark the current default criteria in `measure_sec_suitability()`; they are included to explain the comparison, not to claim method acceptance.", fig.alt = "Two-panel line chart with column age in days on the x-axis. The top panel shows expected plate count decreasing from 45,000 to 32,000 plates; the bottom panel shows expected resolution decreasing from 2.8 to 2.0. Dashed software-default lines mark 5,000 plates and resolution 1.5. All values are synthetic scenario labels, not measurements."}
criteria_lines <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c(
    "Expected plate count (N, plates)",
    "Expected resolution (Rs)"
  ),
  value = c(5000, 1.5)
)

ggplot(run_metrics, aes(x = column_age_days, y = expected_value)) +
  geom_blank(
    data = criteria_lines |> mutate(column_age_days = 0),
    aes(x = column_age_days, y = value),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(group = metric, colour = "Synthetic scenario"),
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = "Synthetic scenario"), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    data = criteria_lines,
    aes(yintercept = value, colour = "Software default"),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Synthetic scenario" = "#2E86AB",
      "Software default" = "#A23B72"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Column age in synthetic example (days)",
    y = "Generated scenario value"
  ) +
  theme_measure_sec()
```

## Calculating suitability from an integration table

`measure_sec_suitability()` accepts a peak table with retention times and
widths. If named reference peaks are supplied, it calculates resolution; it
also calculates plate count from the selected main peak. Tailing, recovery,
and replicate RSD are reported when the corresponding input columns or
arguments are present.

The function's current defaults are resolution at least 1.5, plate count at
least 5,000, tailing factor from 0.8 to 1.5, recovery from 95% to 105%,
retention-time RSD at most 1%, and area RSD at most 2%. These are software
defaults. Select criteria for the method and review the width definitions and
calculation conventions before using the output.

```{r suitability-template, eval=FALSE}
# Replace these objects with the integration table and criteria for your method.
sst <- measure_sec_suitability(
  peaks = integration_peak_table,
  reference_peaks = critical_peak_names,
  criteria = method_criteria
)

print(sst)
```

## Repeatability requires replicate injections

`measure_sec_suitability()` can calculate retention-time and peak-area RSD when
the peak table includes a `replicate` column and named peaks. The synthetic
column-age dataset has no replicate injections, so those RSD values cannot be
calculated from it. Pass replicate-level integration results when evaluating
precision; keep missing results as missing rather than replacing them with
zero.

```{r precision-template, eval=FALSE}
# The table must contain actual repeated injections with peak-level values.
precision_results <- measure_sec_suitability(
  peaks = replicate_peak_table,
  reference_peaks = critical_peak_names,
  criteria = method_criteria
)

precision_results$results$retention_rsd
precision_results$results$area_rsd
```
